newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--A systematic campaign to terrorise the ethnic Greek minority in southern Albania is under way in an effort to avert the expected influx of ethnic Greek-Albanians from Greece into Albania to vote in Sunday's poll. An armed gang yesterday kidnapped a leading member of the community, warning his daughter to withdraw her candidacy for the elections. Another ethnic Greek was kidnapped for ransom in Sarande.

--Economics professor Yiannis Spraos, the architect of the eponymous report on how Greece can achieve convergence, is reported to be working another seven reports on issues ranging from reorganisation of mechanisms to collect revenues to public administration.

--Unionists aligned to ruling party PASOK yesterday criticised the government's economic policies and its handling of 'social dialogue' between government, employers and unionists on changes to the job market.

--The government yesterday leaked information that it would make changes to the tax system next month, increasing the tax-free threshold to 2.5 million drachmas, index-linking the tax scale and changes to tax brackets, including a possible reduction on tax rates for businesses.

--An almost certain European Court decision against Greece over the pricing of imported secondhand cars is pushing down prices on new and old vehicles.The government is working on radical changes to the taxation of cars ahead of the decision.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday criticised the state of television in Greece and called for respect of privacy, during a function to welcome the new members of the Radio and Television Council.
--A well-known department store was the focus of investigation yesterday after dozens of complaints from consumers about the unethical behaviour of its private security guards.

--Greece is considering participating in the peacekeeping force to be sent to Nagorno-Karabakh, National Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos said in New York yesterday. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
